newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf crude lifters expect higher October OSPs.
newsitem.headline: Gulf crude lifters expect higher October OSPs.

text.p: Oman, Abu Dhabi and Qatar are expected to increase their retroactive official selling prices for crude lifted in October, Gulf traders said on Wednesday.
The three Gulf producers are scheduled in the coming days to announce their prices for October when oil prices hit five-year-highs because of low product inventory levels.
"It has to be higher," a manager at a Japanese company based in the Gulf said.
The official prices cover volumes lifted by foreign firms, notably those in Japan, from the Gulf producers.
Reuters' assessment of Oman crude in the Asian spot market has averaged $21.80 a barrel in the first 30 days of this month, compared to an average of $20.75 in September.
Oman's official crude price for September was $21.20, its highest level so far this year and up from its year low of $16.50 for liftings in February.
Gulf regional benchmark crude Dubai has averaged $21.65-70 between October 1-30, up from a September average of $20.35.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's (ADNOC) official September price for Murban stood at $22.30 and Qatar Marine stood at $21.66.
